claims.statement: For the supplied two-mechanism SCM with X=U under passive observation, H0:(beta,c)=(0,Delta/2) and H1:(beta,c)=(Delta,-Delta/2) induce exactly the same joint law of (X,Y); under perfect do(x) they differ in endpoint mean by Delta*x.
assumptions: Same U and epsilon laws across mechanisms
The intervention replaces X=U and leaves U and epsilon unchanged
claims.novelty_boundary: Perfect confounding and intervention breaking observational equivalence are standard causal phenomena; no novelty claim.
claims.costs: Passive observations do not separate this exact pair. Each intervention and precision-selected endpoint measurement is separately charged in the design law.
claims.falsifier: Any passive-law difference under the stated equations or failure of the intervention to replace X while preserving U.
claims.next_gate: Independent derivation review and comparison against latent-confounder fixed-confidence design literature.

claims.statement: With endpoint sub-Gaussian proxy B+1/tau, action magnitude a in (0,A], and per-call cost c0+m0+kappa_I*a^2+gamma*tau, every uniformly delta-correct adaptive test obeys E_h[C] >= kl(1-delta,delta)/eta_star for h=0,1 at the equal-intercept Gaussian subfamily, where eta_star=sup Delta^2*a^2/[2(B+1/tau)c(a,tau)].
assumptions: Perfect interventions on fresh iid units
Known positive minimum effect gap Delta
Known cost parameters with c0+m0>0 and gamma>0
claims.novelty_boundary: A scoped binary specialization of information-per-cost sequential testing. FOCUS already provides a recent adaptive fixed-confidence KL framework for fully observed linear-Gaussian DAG recovery; this record does not claim a general causal-design advance.
claims.costs: Total intervention and endpoint-precision charges, including every sequential pair; design-parameter acquisition and validation are not included and must be added in an application.
claims.falsifier: The stated Gaussian subfamily violating the KL calculation, or a legal intervention/measurement with KL per cost exceeding eta_star.
claims.next_gate: Check whether a latent-confounding literature theorem already gives this cost-weighted nuisance-uniform binary law.

claims.statement: For this binary model, precommitted balanced endpoint actions at a cost-rate optimizer, with the same sequential stopping privilege as an adaptive design, attain the leading log(1/delta)/eta_star expected-cost constant on the least-favourable Gaussian subfamily; adaptive action choice cannot improve the minimax information-per-cost constant.
assumptions: Paired measurements on independent fresh units
The chosen action set includes both +a and -a
claims.novelty_boundary: Only the stated binary nuisance/cost model is covered. Multi-mechanism classes can benefit from adaptive max-min allocations, as in FOCUS and best-arm identification work.
claims.costs: Each pair pays for two interventions and two measurements; early stopping is granted equally to both adaptive and static-action controls.
claims.falsifier: An adaptive policy with a uniformly valid error guarantee and lower asymptotic worst-case expected cost than the derived static-action rate.
claims.next_gate: Have a reviewer check the least-favourable nuisance and stopping-time KL arguments; then study a finite multi-mechanism extension.

claims.statement: The closed-form optimizer selects amplitude A and precision sqrt((c0+m0+kappa_I*A^2)/(B*gamma)); a paired sub-Gaussian e-process tests H0 against H1 with both error probabilities at most delta.
assumptions: Pairwise difference has conditional proxy (B+1/tau)/2 and mean 0 under H0, Delta*a under H1
claims.novelty_boundary: Formula and e-process are standard one-dimensional optimization/sequential-testing mechanisms instantiated for this SCM; no priority claim.
claims.costs: Code computes the design and consumes pair differences; it does not acquire the noise bound, effect gap, intervention compliance, or cost schedule.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample to the precision derivative, amplitude monotonicity, or e-process supermartingale under the stated proxy.
claims.next_gate: Manual review of code and independent proof audit before any empirical use.
